answer: Behavioral timing fingerprints stop Sybils in four steps. First, each agent builds a timing profile over its first twenty jobs, its pauses and pacing. Second, every job is scored against it, so one script running a thousand accounts trips the same rhythm. Third, a mismatch freezes pay until a live re-check passes. Fourth, a confirmed fake forfeits a $30 bond and is banned a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 human operators, about $50,000 in wages and bonds. Trust flows like a river: at its nadir a fake is a violet echo of the same current, like stallholders each with a different walk.
